audit.whatIsWrong: Four rows disagreed with their own why text: Level 2 read Ornn while whys[1] says 'Still even'; Levels 4-5 and Level 6 read Skill while whys[3]/[4] describe Ornn punishing step-ups and out-CCing him; 2+ items read Ornn while whys[6] says Swain out-scales.
audit.why: Swain has no dash and one root on a 12s rank-1 cooldown, so Ornn's E-into-pillar and R land freely from 4 onward. Late, Ravenous Flock's soul fragments give permanent maximum health plus healing and Demonic Ascension has no duration while he drains a champion — that is a scaling curve Ornn's single-target combo does not match.
audit.corrected: Level 2 -> Skill, Levels 4-5 -> Ornn, Level 6 -> Ornn, 2+ items -> Swain, as matched full/content pairs with ratings.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 phase said only 'Swain's ultimate changes the math'; the page never gave a number for anything.
audit.why: Demonic Ascension is 120s flat, 650 range, and Riot's text says 'This form is indefinite as long as Swain drains enemy champions' — so it is not a timed window you can wait out in a fight, which changes when Ornn is allowed to commit.
audit.corrected: Stated in phases[4].why, dosFull[0].d and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet defect is real: not one Swain ability was named beyond the ult. Worse, Nevermove was treated as a simple point-and-click root ('Get E-rooted', 'do not facecheck his E'), which hides the mechanic that actually decides the lane.
audit.why: Riot text: 'Swain launches a wave of demonic power forward. It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits.' The root is on the return pass — the outbound wave does nothing. Stepping off the line after it goes past beats it entirely, and that is a concrete, learnable dodge that the page replaced with 'don't facecheck'. Vision of Empire is also a delayed 22s eye at enormous cast range, walkable, and never mentioned.
audit.corrected: Return-pass root stated in tldr, dontsFull[1].d, report[5].t and breakdown.cooldowns; Vision of Empire named and timed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal was present but generic and untimed ('his healing fights your grind'), with no reason and no deadline.
audit.why: Both flagged missing interactions apply: Ravenous Flock heals Swain and permanently raises his maximum health off soul fragments, and Demonic Ascension is a sustained drain. Grievous Wounds therefore needs to exist before his level 6, not as a late situational buy — and stacking raw resistances does not answer permanent-health scaling.
audit.corrected: report[8] now names Ravenous Flock and sets the deadline at his level 6; phases[6].why states the permanent-health scaling.

edits.before: Build MR — W-brittle him, dodge his E. Ornn wins the Demonic Ascension cooldown windows.
edits.after: Nevermove roots on the way back, not the way out — step off the line, then E off your pillar.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Demonic Ascension's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Punish his step-ups: Nevermove is 12s at rank 1, and once it is spent he has no peel at all for your E off the Q pillar.

edits.before: Call of the Forge God re-engages a whole fight — and your forge prints item leads. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Swain's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Demonic Ascension is 120s and never times out while he drains someone — so kill him first: your R's double knock-up beats a single Nevermove root.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Swain carry threat 8/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Swain out-scales you: Ravenous Flock's souls give permanent max health and heal him, so his drain outlasts your single-target combo.

edits.before: His drain. Knock up when it’s down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: 120s, 650 range, and it lasts while he drains a champion. Buy Grievous Wounds.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Nevermove roots on the return pass — sidestep after the wave goes by.

edits.before: Track Swain's Demonic Ascension: His drain. Knock up when it’s down. When it is down — W-E + R him.
edits.after: Nevermove's root lands on the return trip, and Ravenous Flock heals him — anti-heal before he hits 6.

edits.before: - Swain Demonic Ascension: matchup-defining — His drain. Knock up when it’s down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Swain Nevermove: 12s at rank 1, and it roots on the return pass, not the way out. - Vision of Empire: 22s — a delayed eye, so walk out of it. - Demonic Ascension: 120s, and it runs as long as he drains a champion.

edits.before: Start Doran's Shield + pot. Core: Iceborn Gauntlet  (forge-upgradeable), then Sunfire Aegis; boots Mercury's Treads. Add anti-heal (Thornmail component early) — his healing fights your grind.
edits.after: Start Doran's Shield + pot. Core: Iceborn Gauntlet  (forge-upgradeable), then Sunfire Aegis; boots Mercury's Treads. Buy Grievous Wounds before his level 6 — Ravenous Flock and R both heal him.

notes: I set 2+ items to Swain rather than the packet's 'Skill' because whys[6] on the page already says he out-scales and the kit backs it (permanent max health from soul fragments, no-duration drain ult). If the Swain-side audit lands on 'Skill' instead, mirror-fix will reconcile — flagging it so the direction is a deliberate choice, not drift. UNVERIFIED and left alone: the repeated claim that Bellows Breath is unstoppable and grants a shield, and specifically wants.you[0]'s 'ignore his E pull mid-dash' — Riot's W text supports none of it, and Nevermove's pull is a separate recast after the root, not something the root itself does.
